punchline: Busy readers recommended nearly twice the sentence, because they never got to doubt the false lines.
thirty_sec: In a 1993 experiment, Daniel Gilbert and colleagues had volunteers read crime reports with false lines marked in colour. Distracted volunteers recommended 11.15 years for false aggravating lines versus 5.83 for false excusing ones, while calm readers gave 7.03 and 6.03.
question: Which belief you act on today did you pick up while busy with something else?
key_contrast: Believing arrives first and free, while doubting needs attention.
